newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke - no surrender of tax, spending under EMU.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke - no surrender of tax, spending under EMU.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Monday that the UK would not have to surrender control of tax and public expenditure policy if it signed up for European Economic and Monetary Union.

"There is a pooling of sovereignty involved in transferring monetary authority to a European Central Bank," he told the Treasury Select Committee in parliament. "But there is no transfer of control over taxation, there is no transfer of control over public expenditure."

Clarke added that to join a single currency comprising non-converging economies "would be to run a substantial and unacceptable risk that it was going to cause damage and I would advocate not joining economic and monetary union if the economies of the member states aren't converging."
